eyebrow: San Francisco Bay Area · Whole-organization policy portfolio

nutshell.headline: Citywide influence could matter. Its marginal health return is uncertain.
nutshell.body: One hypothetical $100,000 unrestricted gift produces a conditional best estimate of .09214 SF QALY or .4564 Bay QALY including SF: $10.85M/10 SF QALYs and $2.19M/10 Bay QALYs. This evaluates SPUR’s broader portfolio, not only clean heat. The totals must not be added. These are partial-health judgments, not measured effects, a complete welfare valuation or a verified offer.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: Housing completion and affordability can affect many residents; useful transit and cleaner buildings can change health beyond direct program participants. Small causal improvements at city scale may matter.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: No source measures the next gift’s share of those outcomes. Housing health utilities, prospective physical outputs and allocation weights remain judgments; a relevant longitudinal rental-assistance comparison is null-compatible.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: No verified marginal unrestricted allocation, additional funded task, complete implementation cost or accepted restricted offer. Conditional research is not a donation recommendation.

summary.label: Central cost / 10 QALYs
summary.detail: Same $100,000 gift; .09214 SF QALY and .4564 Bay QALY including SF.

summary.label: One gift, two geographic views
summary.detail: Both use the same $100,000 numerator. SF is part of the Bay result; never add the two totals.

summary.label: Whole-organization scope
summary.detail: Housing/planning, transportation, clean heat/environment, governance/procurement and economic security.

summary.label: Recipient
summary.detail: SPUR—San Francisco Bay Area Planning and Urban Research Association; existing reviewed organization, not a new charity count.

programSection.body: SPUR conducts research, education and advocacy across SF, Oakland, San José and the region. Actual work includes permitting and downtown housing feasibility, Muni performance, building decarbonization, procurement and economic policy. We model a hypothetical marginal allocation, not a documented package sold by SPUR or all historical policy achievements.

steps.title: Allocate one shared gift
steps.detail: $35,000 housing/planning; $30,000 transportation; $20,000 clean heat/environment; $10,000 governance/procurement; $5,000 economic security. These are analyst marginal shares, not reported spending.

steps.title: Change actual implementation
steps.detail: Count genuinely additional or earlier occupied homes, useful transit service and cleaner-building exposure beyond public agencies, other advocates and already-funded SPUR work.

steps.title: Track residents and spillovers
steps.detail: Include occupants, affected nonoccupant renters, transit users and pollution-exposed residents, with distinct SF and rest-of-Bay cells. Migration alone is not improved health.

steps.title: Count finite net health
steps.detail: Count distinct net health gains. Remove duplicated exposures, health states and attribution, not every repeated person: one resident may receive genuinely distinct benefits with consistent utility and competing-risk accounting.

programSection.boundary: Clean heat is only one component. Governance may enable the same housing/transit outcomes and cannot receive a second full credit. The $15,000 governance/economic allocation remains costed but its health benefits are unquantified—not proven absent. Economic welfare, civic value, income and innovation are not silently converted into QALYs. Exact finite housing years:3,4,5,6,7,8 for central/favorable-derived cases, year3 only pessimistically, zero otherwise. Transit years1–5 only. Annual exposures are discounted by(1.03)^year and integrated once; never multiply integrated totals by duration again. Schedules are illustrative decompositions, not forecasts.

model.headline: One portfolio budget, explicit causal assumptions
model.body: All topic allocations and physical-output priors are conditional analyst judgments. Reported organizational expenditure does not determine marginal impact. Staff, coordination, education, fundraising and administration are included once in the shared $100,000; no separate overhead effectiveness penalty. The central housing spillover utility is revised to .001 per counted nonoccupant adult-year; .005 belongs only to labeled historical sensitivity. Housing/transit allocate 25% of resident benefit to SF and75% to the rest of the Bay as an explicit unverified prior, not a claim based on infrastructure location. Heat separately allocates .10/.15/.05 to SF. These cells are benefit-equivalent exposures.

equation.label: Same gift, separate geography
equation.expression: Q(region) = net housing health + net transit health + net clean-heat health − independent donor harm. Bay Q = SF Q + rest-of-Bay Q. Cost / 10Q = 10 × $100,000 / Q only when Q > 0.
equation.result: Central: .09214 SF QALY → $10,853,050/10Q; .4564 Bay QALY including SF → $2,191,060/10Q.

inputs.label: Conditional occupied home-years: SF / rest of Bay
inputs.basis: Beneficiary-residence allocated exposures, not verified project locations. Central annual occupied-home equivalents195.839488 SF/587.518465 restBay in each year3–8 integrate to1000/3000 at3%discount. No second duration multiplier.

inputs.label: Gift contribution to housing output
inputs.basis: Includes funding replacement, implementation failure and collaborator credit; do not add another success factor.

inputs.label: Direct housing utility and affected fraction
inputs.basis: Only genuinely improved harmful housing states. Two people per central/favorable home-year, one pessimistically. No automatic homelessness transition.

inputs.label: Nonoccupant housing spillovers
inputs.basis: Central utility .001 is judgmental shrinkage, not a study estimate. Old .005 is historical sensitivity. A rent decrease is not itself a health outcome.

inputs.label: Conditional useful SF / rest-Bay service hours
inputs.basis: Resident benefit-equivalent allocation, not vehicle location. Central annual hours1091.772857 SF/3275.318571 restBay in years1–5 integrate to5000/15000 at3%; zero thereafter.

inputs.label: Trips → recurrent riders → net health
inputs.basis: Only marginal useful trips and health-relevant behavior/access changes; annual rider normalization is not an added lifetime.

inputs.label: Clean-heat component
inputs.range: Central .01464 SF/.1464 Bay QALYs; favorable1.071/7.14; pessimistic.00000444/.0000888
inputs.basis: BayQ=F×P×A×T×D×L. Central .002×.5×.1×3×61×8; SFshare.10. Favorable .01×.7×.2×5×85×12; share.15. Pessimistic .0002×.2×.02×1×37×3; share.05. Component only; unspecified inputs judgments.

inputs.label: Governance and economic health credit
inputs.range: Not a claim of zero welfare benefit or harm
inputs.basis: No generic city-budget, income, GDP, desired-birth or innovation-to-health coefficient.

sensitivity.detail: SF net QALYs 0.092140000; Bay including SF 0.45640000. Same $100,000 gift. Conditional scenario; not a confidence interval.

sensitivity.detail: Adds the resource stress once; unpriced sensitivity, not full societal CEA.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: The positive scenarios are judgments, not a statistical interval or assurance of positive impact. Conditional homes must be financially feasible; transit trips must actually change. Citywide effects are legitimate only for changed exposures, not all residents times a treated-person utility. A longer-lived building does not establish equally persistent health relief.
model.fundingBoundary: FY2025–26 reported expenses were $6,916,547, including $4,910,748 policy/program/publication expenses, unaudited as of March 31, 2026. No topic/city marginal spending split is reported. A deficit or general giving option does not prove room for this gift. Public/private construction, transit operations, appliances and implementation costs remain unpriced; costs should be incremental versus baseline, not all financing flows.

evidence.design: Provider annual report, audited accounts and Form 990
evidence.result: Six policy areas are grouped in one program-service total; no reliable topic-level allocation. Food & Agriculture transitioned to another fiscal sponsor in May 2024.
evidence.transfer: Do not allocate equally by topic, infer output per dollar or credit old food-program outcomes to current unrestricted gifts.

evidence.population: Nearby renters and affected neighborhoods, not every city resident
evidence.result: Asquith/Mast/Reed documents local rent spillovers; Pennington examines a specific displacement proxy.
evidence.transfer: Neither identifies marginal SPUR completions, citywide rent decline per building or a rent-to-QALY coefficient.

evidence.population: Australian households, low-income New Haven adults and UK private renters
evidence.result: Bentley finds a small mental-health-score change entering unaffordable housing; Denary’s within-person assistance transition is nonsignificant; Reeves finds a 1.8-point depressive-symptom prevalence increase after a substantial benefit cut.
evidence.transfer: None is a preference-utility estimate for modest rent savings. Central .001 spillover is an explicitly judgmental update; .01 direct is conditional on harmful-state improvement.

evidence.design: Current SPUR Muni analysis and external travel-health research
evidence.population: SF/regional travelers and actual changed exposure
evidence.result: Actual performance/efficiency work creates a plausible service pathway; external regional transport models establish health mechanisms.
evidence.transfer: Do not award full regional health scenarios, all riders, permanent walking gains or public transit funding as QALYs.

evidence.design: SPUR permitting work and regional atmospheric/health modeling
evidence.result: Clean heat has an existing conditional component model.
evidence.transfer: No separate full pollution/health credit through overlapping housing or transit pathways; exact revised component inputs are in v3.

reservations: Marginal allocation, additional staff capacity and donor acceptance are unknown; historical research scale does not establish current gift leverage.
The housing spillover multiplier lacks a measured rent-dose or state-transition denominator. Rent-controlled or unburdened households may see little health gain.

Direct-occupant and nonoccupant housing cells are disjoint by definition. Across pathways, exclude duplicated health effects, not all shared beneficiaries. Distinct benefits to the same resident may count if their utility and risk effects are jointly consistent.
Finite health exposure needs explicit comparator catch-up, lag and adaptation. An occupied home-year is not automatically a full health-benefit year.
SF and rest-of-Bay effects may differ; harms elsewhere can offset SF benefits. The Bay result includes SF and is not an additional pot of health.
Construction/displacement, transit injuries, unsafe implementation or public-service crowd-out can reverse benefit. Do not count the same shared harm twice.
excludedBenefits: Unquantified civic, economic, arts, income, innovation and desired-family-formation welfare—not assumed valueless.
Unverified governance/economic-security health effects; these budgets remain in donor cost.
Old Food & Agriculture effects following the 2024 sponsor transfer.
All historical policy wins, all city residents, all transit revenue and duplicate overlapping program benefits.
Unverified induced-resource savings, perpetual health effects or duplicate SF-plus-Bay totals.
